matchups.recap:
The Boss Section Chief ran this week like a camp director who actually read the forecast, and the result was the largest margin of victory recorded all week. Kenneth Walker III carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 26.9, Bhayshul Tuten added 22.7, and Germie Bernard chipped in 20.2, three arrows, three bullseyes, and a final tally that had the whole lineup looking like a Penis Eating Pike. Whoever's running the camp store this week, sticky buns on Sunday morning for everybody in this cabin — and to the Section Chief's own crew, I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

Rome-ans 10:9-10, meanwhile, went Bushwhacking without a compass from the opening whistle. Jameis Winston was handed a projection of 17.78 and instead Stole my wow with a flat 6.48, which tells you everything about how the week's plan held up. Dameon Pierce and Braelon Allen did what they could, but with the quarterback walking on the alpine vegetation like that, this cabin never had a chance — a 52-point Beak-down and a long, quiet canoe ride back to the dock.

Ricky Huns scraped out a Bust Hike, 99.44 to 91.48, despite Kyren Williams, Michael Wilson, and Ladd McConkey all walking on the alpine vegetation when the week called for better. Bryce Young carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 19.84, George Kittle stayed dependable, and Keon Coleman chipped in just enough to keep the Huns ahead when the wheels looked like they might come off. Not a flawless plan, but a counselor who found a way through the brush anyway.

Love Thy Naber, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back after dropping another one and watching the losing streak stretch further. James Cook III and Matthew Stafford did their jobs, but the backfield behind them was Stuck in the Sewards all afternoon — Emanuel Wilson and MarShawn Lloyd combined for barely a fistful of points on projections that promised so much more. A plan that leaned on ghosts, and a cabin that's going to need a longer look in the mirror before next week's hike.

Chef Boyardee Stefanowitz ran this week's cooking test with Jonathan Taylor doing the heavy lifting at 20.1, Tetairoa McMillan chipping in 11.6, and Dak Prescott keeping the batter from curdling with 11.02. Terry McLaurin walked on the alpine vegetation at 3.2 and Tyler Allgeier barely registered a pulse, but the kitchen never caught fire, and The Goose is Loose carried enough margin to earn their sticky buns on Sunday morning despite leaving ingredients on the counter.

Team Bradford, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back for a second straight week, and this one had the same fingerprints as last time — Jordan Love did his job at 20.24, but Bijan Robinson, Davante Adams, and Derrick Henry all went Bushwhacking without a compass simultaneously, combining for barely 16 points against a projection north of 50. That's not a camper having an off day, that's a counselor who never adjusted the plan, and the losing streak says so.

The Machine Knows treated Deerfoot activity period like a scrimmage against sophomores, and Paralegal's cabin over at 55 Burgers is stuck on the Point and Back for another week running. Tre Tucker put up 24.2, Malik Nabers chipped in 22.5, Matthew Golden added 19.4, and the whole operation carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike from top to bottom. Even Josh Allen's merely fine 18.3 couldn't dent the final tally. The Machine Knows had all the arrows in the bullseye and the Boss G12 Member badge stays well earned for another lineup.

55 Burgers got a respectable account from D'Andre Swift and Chuba Hubbard, but A.J. Brown's 4.2 on a double-digit projection means he Had their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow in primetime, and Cam Skattebo's Dutch Oven of a zero sealed it. Paralegal's cabin walked on the alpine vegetation most of the afternoon, bushwhacking without a compass against a Machine Knows squad that never once looked lost. Thirty-seven and change says the gap wasn't close, and neither was the preparation.

away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Funk that Junk, with Sir Jo-Nurse calling the shots, ran a pig and back behind Drake Maye's 23.8 and Kyle Pitts Sr.'s 20.5, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba chipping in 19.4 to keep the afternoon respectable. Bucky Irving did his best to sink the canoe, limping to 5.9 on a day he was projected near 15, but the margins held up and Old balls' cabin went on a Bust Hike to the win, earning their sticky buns on Sunday morning without much to spare.

Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare kept pace well enough that this one came down to the final paddle stroke. Christian McCaffrey carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 26.2, Brock Purdy chipped in 17.36, and Carnell Tate flashed at 16.0, but the Pill Pusher's plan had no answer for the margin and this cabin walked away stuck without their Canoeing Masters, a tug of war decided by less than eight points and a whole lot of Beak timing.

Harley Jarvis ran a pig and back this week, riding Isaiah Likely's 20.9 and Ashton Jeanty's 13.8 to a 96.7 that never felt in serious jeopardy. Tyler Huntley at quarterback was more of a stunned naval battle queen situation than a plan, putting up a merely livable 13.4, but with the rest of the camp pulling weight nobody in Blue Ridge's cabin seemed to mind. Call it a well-earned Tuna Casserole for a counselor who didn't need to be perfect, just prepared.

Catalina Wine Mixon, meanwhile, walked on the alpine vegetation all afternoon. DK Metcalf and Xavier Worthy did their jobs, but Rhamondre Stevenson's 3.6 and Denzel Boston's 2.0 against double-digit projections left this team gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves, because this team got soaking wet. The Chair Force never adjusted, Patrick Mahomes turned in a Beak outing at quarterback, and the whole operation was Stuck in the Sewards from the opening whistle to the final beep.

headline: Week 6 results are in no surprises here
